title: The Best Pair of Sights Along the Road

concept.title: Split the score into a part that depends on i and a part that depends on j
body: Along a road there are `n` sights, the sight `i` is worth `a[i]` and stands at the distance `i` from the start. A visitor picks two sights `i < j`, and the score of the pair is the sum of their values **minus the distance between them**: `a[i] + a[j] - (j - i)`. Find the best score. For the values `8 1 5 2 6` the pair at the positions 0 and 2 scores 8 + 5 - 2 = 11.

Trying all pairs is O(n^2). Rewrite the score as **`(a[i] + i) + (a[j] - j)`**: the first part depends only on `i`, the second only on `j`. Walk along the road with `j`; for each `j` the best partner `i < j` is the one with the **largest `a[i] + i` among the earlier sights**. So keep that maximum as you go: `left = max(left, a[j] + j)` after using it.

body.code:
best = 0
left = a[0]                         # the largest a[i] + i among the sights before j
for j in range(1, n):
    best = max(best, left + a[j] - j)
    left = max(left, a[j] + j)
print(best)

body: The running maximum `left` is a tiny DP: `left(j) = max(left(j - 1), a[j - 1] + j - 1)`. Splitting a score into independent parts, so that a prefix maximum can be used, is the standard way to speed up "best pair" problems from O(n^2) to O(n). The result can reach 2 * 10^9, so use 64-bit numbers.

statement: Along a road there are `n` sights; the sight `i` (counting from 0) has the value `a[i]`. The score of a pair of sights `i < j` is `a[i] + a[j] - (j - i)`. Print the largest score of a pair.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of sights.
The second line has `n` numbers: the value of each sight, in the order along the road.
hints: Write the score as (a[i] + i) + (a[j] - j).
For each j the best i is the one with the largest a[i] + i before j.
Keep that maximum while walking along the road.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: The score a[i] + a[j] - (j - i) equals (a[i] + i) + (a[j] - j), so for every j the best i is the one with the largest a[i] + i before it; this maximum is kept while walking along the road.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

best = 0
left = a[0]
for j in range(1, n):
    best = max(best, left + a[j] - j)
    left = max(left, a[j] + j)
print(best)
